mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly says 'X has N more than Y', translate it to X = Y + N (add N to Y).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any direct count statement of the form 'X has N more than Y'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has N more than Y' as X = N instead of X = Y + N.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: For a transfer statement 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement describing a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Treating a transfer as adding N to both X and Y, or subtracting from the wrong person.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person, translate every statement into a linear equation (or inequality), and solve the resulting system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains multiple relational statements that together determine the unknowns.
mathgap.example: Skipping the creation of equations and guessing values.

mathgap.title: Combined sum interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'X has N more than Y and Z combined', first sum Y and Z, then add N: X = (Y + Z) + N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement that compares X to the combined total of two or more other persons.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has N more than Y and Z combined' as X = Y + N, ignoring Z.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times', multiply the original amount by k to get the new amount.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement describing a multiplicative increase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'increases by 2 times' as adding 2 instead of multiplying by 2.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and each recipient receives the splitter's original count divided equally.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement describing an equal split of items among multiple recipients.
mathgap.example: Leaving the splitter's count unchanged after a split.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: When a statement uses the phrase 'difference between X and Y' (without qualifiers like 'absolute'), interpret it as the signed difference X - Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement that mentions the difference between two persons.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between X and Y' as |X - Y|, losing sign information.

mathgap.title: Sequential statement processing
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given: direct count statements set the current count at that point, transfers adjust those counts, and relational equations refer to the current counts after previous updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any problem where the order of statements matters, especially with transfers.
mathgap.example: Applying a relational equation before a transfer that changes the involved counts.

mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: When a relational statement says 'the number of X that Y has more than Z' (or similar) without a numeric offset, interpret it as a signed difference Y - Z and set up the equation (Y - Z) = (some expression). Do not treat it as a direct count or as an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any relational statement equating a 'has more than' expression to another difference.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'The number of potatoes that Minerva has more than Louella is equal to the difference between Lydia and Morgan' as Minerva = Louella + (Lydia - Morgan) instead of Minerva - Louella = Lydia - Morgan.

mathgap.description: Treating 'X has N' as an initial count before transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that a direct count statement fixes the final amount, ignoring later transfer statements that modify the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply transfers after establishing the initial count, updating the giver's and receiver's amounts accordingly.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often leaves the splitter's count unchanged or distributes items incorrectly.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement says a person splits all items equally among recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient an equal share of the original amount.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may add the transferred amount to the giver or subtract it from the receiver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'X has more than Y' as |X‑Y| or as a direct count, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret such expressions as signed differences (X‑Y) and keep the sign when forming equations.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the order of subtraction, turning a signed difference into a non‑negative value.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always treat 'difference between X and Y' as the signed expression X‑Y (first name minus second).
